The open question

None physical, and one economic. Gas on Venus is a commodity — CO₂ and N₂ are unlimited, fungible and worth nothing per unit, and nobody can corner them. Gravity is the opposite: not transferable, not storable, not tradeable, and therefore not a commodity at all. It is a premium attached to a location, which means it cannot be de-fungibilised because it was never fungible, and cannot be speculated on because it cannot change hands. The only way to hold it is to be standing there.
